source: &73 Having been here for some time...this is more of a waiting room.
target: &73 在这里待了一阵子之后……我觉得，这更像一间等候室。

source: &644 Wait, why'd you think I was Viksha...Dr Perera?
target: &644 等等，你为什么以为我是维克莎……佩雷拉博士？

source: &74 The family resemblance is unmistakable.
target: &74 你们家族的相似之处，实在太明显了。

source: &645 How can you see my face? We're in the Trance!
target: &645 你怎么看得到我的脸？我们在迷境里！

source: &75 I see your mind, my dear.
target: &75 我看到的是你的心智，亲爱的。

source: &76 Of that similarity, there can be no confusion.
target: &76 那种相似，不可能认错。

source: &646 Who are you, exactly?
target: &646 你到底是谁？

source: &77 Adam Baxter, PhD.
target: &77 亚当·巴克斯特，博士。

source: &78 Delighted to meet you, Ms...Mandala, was it?
target: &78 很高兴认识你，小姐……是叫曼荼罗吧？

source: &647 You're...Baxter...?
target: &647 你是……巴克斯特……？

source: &79 Quite so. Or...I believe as such.
target: &79 正是。或者说……我想我是。

source: &648 You're his memories...that Mindjacker stole your consciousness!
target: &648 你是他的记忆……那个意识劫持者偷走了你的意识！

source: &80 That is an interesting theory, my dear.
target: &80 一个有趣的理论，亲爱的。

source: &649 What are all these ghosts?
target: &649 那些幽灵是什么？

source: &650 They're just standing there...staring...
target: &650 就站在那里……盯着看……

source: &81 I've been putting my mind, or what's left of it, to the question.
target: &81 我一直在用自己的心智，或者剩下的那点心智，思考这个问题。

source: &82 If this is a waiting room...there might perhaps be other "guests"?
target: &82 如果这里是等候室……也许他们是其他的“客人”？

source: &651 They aren't nearly as detailed as what's left of you.
target: &651 他们远没有剩下的你这么完整。

source: &652 Maybe they needed more of YOUR mind than of theirs?
target: &652 也许，他们从你的心智里取走的内容，比其他人更多？

source: &83 Perhaps the watchers have merely resigned themselves to their fate.
target: &83 也许，那些旁观者已经接受了自己的命运。

source: &653 You killed my mother!
target: &653 你杀了我母亲！

source: &654 In the lab! You killed Vicky Perera!
target: &654 在实验室里！你杀了维琪·佩雷拉！

source: &84 I did? I'm sorry, my dear -
target: &84 我杀了？对不起，亲爱的——

source: &85 I have no recollection of such a thing.
target: &85 我完全不记得这种事。

source: &655 I guess they didn't take those memories from you.
target: &655 看来，他们没从你那里取走那些记忆。

source: &86 One ought to remember something as significant as that.
target: &86 这么重要的事，一个人应该记得才对。

source: &656 I guess I've only got Dr Regis' word to go on, now.
target: &656 现在，我也只能听里吉斯博士的一面之词了。

source: &87 Regis...!
&657 Is there a way out of here?
target: &657 有办法离开这里吗？

source: &88 All I can see is nothingness, filled with icosohedral cages.
target: &88 我只看得到虚无，到处都是二十面体的笼子。

source: &89 Although...the way YOU feel...
target: &89 不过……你给我的感觉……

source: &658 Me? I feel fine...
target: &658 我？我感觉挺好……

source: &90 No...you are pulling us, drawing us in...
target: &90 不……你在拉着我们，吸引我们过去……

source: &91 As though YOU are where WE ought to be going...
target: &91 就好像你才是我们该去的地方……

source: &659 There's no way out through me.
target: &659 从我这边出不去。

source: &660 Dead end at my brain.
target: &660 到我的脑子就到头了。

source: &661 Oh nuke...that's the whole point!
target: &661 哦，该炸的……原来就是为了这个！

source: &662 You know Dr Regis?
target: &662 你认识里吉斯博士？

source: &92 That name is an all-consuming catalyst of hatred...
target: &92 那个名字，会激起吞噬一切的仇恨……

source: &93 ...but I can't for the life of me remember why.
target: &93 ……可我怎么也想不起原因。

source: &663 You killed his wife - his evidence put you away for twenty years.
target: &663 你杀了他的妻子，他提供的证据让你坐了二十年牢。

source: &664 And, apparently, he's my father.
target: &664 而且，显然他是我父亲。

source: &94 Hm. It feels as though, for many years, I've wanted nothing more than to...strangle the life out of him.
target: &94 嗯。我感觉，很多年来，我唯一想做的就是……亲手掐死他。

source: &95 But while I know I hate him...I do not understand why.
target: &95 可我虽然知道自己恨他……却不明白为什么。

source: &665 What *can* you remember?
target: &665 那你*还记得*什么？

source: &96 Hm...professional memory. I could relate much of my academic career to you.
target: &96 嗯……专业上的记忆。我能告诉你许多自己学术生涯中的事。

source: &666 What about your time in prison?
target: &666 你坐牢的那段时间呢？

source: &97 ...I was in prison?
target: &97 ……我坐过牢？

source: &667 How about your childhood?
&98 Nothing. This is most troubling, I must say.
target: &98 什么也没有。我得说，这实在令人不安。

source: &668 Obviously Galatea decided they didn't need those memories.
target: &668 显然，伽拉忒亚认为那些记忆没用。

source: &669 Anything else?
target: &669 还有别的吗？

source: &99 That is a difficult question to answer.
target: &99 这个问题很难回答。

source: &100 It's only by looking for memory that one knows it isn't there.
target: &100 只有试着回忆，才会发现记忆已经不在了。

source: &101 Everything else is just...feelings...shreds, here and there.
target: &101 其他的都只是……感觉……零零散散的碎片。

source: &670 You've still got enough to be cognant.
target: &670 剩下的这些，还是足够让你保有意识。

source: &102 An interesting philosophical issue.
target: &102 一个有趣的哲学问题。

source: &103 How much memory is needed for the threshold of "consciousness"?
target: &103 要有多少记忆，才算达到“意识”的门槛？

source: &671 The personalities in here...the "ghosts"...
target: &671 这里的人格……这些“幽灵”……

source: &672 I'm connected to a system that's trying to upload them into my wiring, my brain!
target: &672 我接入的系统，正试着把他们上传进我的神经接口、我的脑子！

source: &104 Myself included, it would appear.
target: &104 看来，也包括我。

source: &105 I have enough awareness to understand that this is not a desirable situation for you.
target: &105 我还保留着足够的意识，能够理解：这不是你想要的局面。

source: &673 You think?!
target: &673 还用你说？！

source: &106 I shall do what I can to slow them.
target: &106 我会尽力拖慢他们。

source: &107 You must find a way to freeze the march of the mind-states.
target: &107 你必须想办法，让这些意识状态停止前进。

source: &674 I've got to figure this out...
target: &674 我得想出办法……

source: &108 Don't wander too far.
target: &108 别走太远。

source: &2 You're right, I'm Viksha Perera - Vicky.
target: &2 没错，我是维克莎·佩雷拉，叫我维琪就好。

source: &3 Dr Vargas mentioned me?
target: &3 瓦尔加斯博士提过我？

source: &2 Wouldn't shut up about you.
target: &2 三句不离你。

source: &3 Like you were Watson, Crick and Einstein rolled into one.
target: &3 说得你好像是沃森、克里克和爱因斯坦合起来一样。

source: &2 ...or more like Oppenheimer, perhaps?
target: &2 ……也许，更像奥本海默？

source: &4 Hey, what we did before isn't the key point.
target: &4 嘿，过去做过什么，不是重点。

source: &5 It's what we can do with the skills we've brought with us.
target: &5 重点是，我们能用带来的本领做些什么。

source: &4 Alright then. What's your field?
target: &4 好吧。那么，你的研究领域是什么？

source: &6 Organic computing, mostly. I studied under Dr Vargas.
target: &6 主要是有机计算。我师从瓦尔加斯博士。

source: &3 Ah, we've probably got some overlap, then.
target: &3 啊，那我们的研究大概有些交集。

source: &7 You look familiar, Doctor...?
target: &7 您看起来有些眼熟，博士……怎么称呼？

source: &4 Nina Jeong, pleased to meet you.
target: &4 妮娜·郑，很高兴认识你。

source: &5 AI and synthetic awareness studies.
target: &5 研究AI与合成人意识。

source: &8 I remember, Dr Vargas was a big fan of your work.
target: &8 我想起来了，瓦尔加斯博士很欣赏您的研究。

source: &5 He's assembling his dream-team.
target: &5 他正在组建自己的梦之队。

source: &6 That's what you get with an absurdly huge grant.
target: &6 拿到一笔大得离谱的研究经费，就能做到这些。

source: &7 Not that I'm complaining.
target: &7 当然，我可没在抱怨。

source: &9 And you are...?
&8 Dr Zvidzai Chigwa. My friends call me Gwen.
target: &8 兹维扎伊·奇格瓦博士。朋友们都叫我格温。

source: &9 I was brought in from Bulaweyo.
target: &9 我是从布拉瓦约招来的。

source: &10 What was your field?
target: &10 您的研究领域是什么？

source: &10 Embryonic baseline engineering.
target: &10 胚胎基础工程。

source: &6 She's a real artist, building new animals from scratch.
target: &6 她可是个艺术家，能从零开始创造新的动物。

source: &11 Angiosperms, mostly. Still not sure why I'm here.
target: &11 主要是被子植物。我还没弄清，为什么找我来。

source: &12 You got any idea what's going on?
target: &12 你知道这是怎么回事吗？

source: &7 Come on, you're the only one of us who's met Vargas in person.
target: &7 拜托，我们几个里，只有你见过瓦尔加斯本人。

source: &8 Do you have any idea what's going on?
target: &8 你知道这是怎么回事吗？

source: &11 I couldn't help you, I'm afraid.
target: &11 恐怕我也帮不上忙。

source: &9 Aw, you're killing us!
target: &9 哎呀，真让人急死了！

source: &13 You expect us to believe he didn't tell his star pupil?
target: &13 你可是他的得意门生，难道他都没告诉你？

source: &12 Well...I might know...
target: &12 嗯……我也许知道一点……

source: &13 But I know how theatrical he can be.
target: &13 可我知道，他这个人有多爱摆排场。

source: &14 It'd mean a lot to him to be the one to reveal it.
target: &14 对他来说，能亲自揭晓这件事，会很重要。

source: &14 Whatever it is, this is some impressive hardware they've got.
target: &14 不管是什么，他们这里的硬件确实很厉害。

source: &15 That, and the secrecy, says "government work" to me.
target: &15 再加上这保密程度，我觉得肯定是“政府项目”。

source: &15 I'll leave you to it.
target: &15 那不打扰你们了。

source: &1 You must be the famous Dr Perera I've been hearing so much about.
target: &1 您一定就是佩雷拉博士吧？久闻大名了。

source: &1 Famous?
target: &1 久闻大名？

source: &1 The way Dr Vargas has been going on, you must have been his star pupil.
target: &1 听瓦尔加斯博士说话的样子，您肯定是他的得意门生。

source: &83 Dr Vargas?
target: &83 瓦尔加斯博士？

source: &1 In here, my dear.
target: &1 在这里，亲爱的。

source: &84 What are you doing?
target: &84 你在做什么？

source: &31 Brodman 9 and 46.
target: &31 布罗德曼第9区和46区。

source: &204 Dr Chigwa is mapping my brain activity.
target: &204 奇格瓦博士正在测绘我的脑活动。

source: &205 In many ways, our product will share more in common with us than other computer platforms.
target: &205 在很多方面，我们的产物跟我们自身的共同点，会比其他计算平台更多。

source: &32 Intermittent rostro-caudal axis patterns.
target: &32 头尾轴的活动模式间歇出现。

source: &33 Tell me - what do you think would be the best manner to train such an AI?
target: &33 告诉我，你觉得怎样训练这种人工智能最好？

source: &85 Naturally. It can handle abstractions better than conventional AI.
target: &85 顺其自然。它处理抽象概念的能力，比传统人工智能更强。

source: &86 Plus, we have millennia of experience and tradition when it comes to education.
target: &86 况且，在教育方面，我们有数千年的经验和传统。

source: &206 I somewhat agree with you. Do you hear that, Gwen?
target: &206 我多少赞同你的观点。听到了吗，格温？

source: &34 Mmhmm...
&207 Though Dr Chigwa agrees that conventional "programming" is impossible...
target: &207 虽然奇格瓦博士也承认，传统的“编程”行不通……

source: &208 ...she is considering the possibility of imprinting existing mind-states within the platform.
target: &208 ……但她在考虑，能否将现成的意识状态写入这个平台。

source: &87 "Quick" for the AI, but utilizing a person's natural experience?
target: &87 对人工智能来说很“快”，但利用的是人自然积累的经验？

source: &209 Though it may not be my philosophical ideal, it is an intriguing experiment.
target: &209 虽然这不太符合我在哲学上的理想，却是个有趣的实验。

source: &210 Ah, it is good to be working with you again, Dr Perera - I mean, Dr *Regis*.
target: &210 啊，能再次与你共事真好，佩雷拉博士。我是说，*里吉斯*博士。

source: &211 Congratulations again, on the wedding.
target: &211 再次祝你新婚快乐。

source: &88 This AI platform will operate billions of times more quickly than the human brain.
target: &88 这个人工智能平台的运作速度，将是人脑的数十亿倍。

source: &89 Frankly, not taking advantage of its superiority would be a waste of time and energy.
target: &89 坦白说，不利用它的优势，才是浪费时间和精力。

source: &212 Do you hear that, Gwen? She agrees with you!
target: &212 听到了吗，格温？她赞同你！

source: &90 Conventional programming is impossible though, isn't it?
target: &90 不过，传统编程行不通，是吧？

source: &91 You couldn't code Central any more than a human brain.
target: &91 不能给人脑写代码，也就不能给中枢写代码。

source: &213 Perhaps, though Dr Baxter believes he may have found a compromise.
target: &213 也许吧，不过巴克斯特博士认为，他可能找到了折中的办法。

source: &214 By mimicking human brain activity, he is seeking to use our own experience as a template.
target: &214 他正在尝试模仿人脑活动，把我们自己的经验作为模板。

source: &92 Giving the AI the experience of human lifetimes, taking advantage of the similarity of the brain structures.
target: &92 利用脑结构的相似性，让人工智能得到人一生的经验。

source: &215 An intriguing thought experiment, don't you think?
target: &215 一个有趣的思想实验，你不觉得吗？

source: &93 It's been too long since Buenos Aires, Eduardo.
target: &93 在布宜诺斯艾利斯之后，我们已经好久没见了，爱德华多。

source: &216 You were my brightest student, Viksha.
target: &216 你曾是我最出色的学生，维克莎。

source: &217 I felt so conflicted when you were awarded that field position.
target: &217 你得到那份外勤工作时，我心里十分矛盾。

source: &94 That feels like so long ago. I was ready for something more sedentary.
target: &94 感觉已经是很久以前了。我已经想换份安定些的工作。

source: &95 And this project - it's like nothing else I've ever worked on before!
target: &95 而这个项目，跟我以前做过的完全不同！

source: &96 It's ground-breaking; the next big step in artificial intelligence!
target: &96 它开创了全新的方向，是人工智能的下一个重大突破！

source: &97 When you mentioned the opening on this project, I couldn't resist.
target: &97 你提到这个项目有空缺时，我实在无法拒绝。

source: &218 You do not know how much I hoped I'd get you for it!
target: &218 你不知道，我有多希望能请到你！

source: &98 It was the right kind of thing, at the right time.
target: &98 正好是在合适的时候，遇到了合适的机会。

source: &99 Sure, fieldwork was great, but sometimes...
target: &99 外勤工作当然很好，可有时候……

source: &219 ...there's nowhere quite like a decent laboratory. I understand, my dear.
target: &219 ……哪里都比不上一间像样的实验室。我明白，亲爱的。

source: &100 After how we split, I was kind of surprised you sought me out.
target: &100 当初不欢而散，你还来找我，我有点惊讶。

source: &220 I admit, when you left Buenos Aires, my emotions took hold of me.
target: &220 我承认，你离开布宜诺斯艾利斯时，我被情绪冲昏了头。

source: &221 We both said many things that I am sure we each regret.
target: &221 我们当时都说了许多话，我相信，彼此现在都后悔。

source: &101 I don't regret taking the field position for one minute, though.
target: &101 不过，接受那份外勤工作，我一刻也没后悔过。

source: &222 Of course. We are lucky to have you with us in Newton.
target: &222 当然。你能来牛顿市跟我们共事，是我们的幸运。

source: &102 When I learned what you were planning to create here, I couldn't resist.
target: &102 得知你们想在这里造出什么以后，我就无法拒绝了。

source: &103 I'm really grateful you could take Charlie on board.
target: &103 你愿意让查理加入，我真的很感激。

source: &223 I can see how much he means to you, Dr Regis!
target: &223 里吉斯博士，我看得出，他对你有多重要！

source: &224 Your opinion and welfare means a great deal to me.
target: &224 你的意见和幸福，对我也十分重要。

source: &225 Of course, I would not have taken him if I did not think him capable.
target: &225 当然，如果不认为他有能力，我也不会让他加入。

source: &104 You've gathered quite an...unconventional team for this project.
target: &104 你为这个项目组建的团队，真是……不同寻常。

source: &226 That is a very tactful way of putting it!
target: &226 这种说法很委婉！

source: &227 I wished for experts who might have a different perspective on matters.
target: &227 我想找些看问题角度不同的专家。

source: &105 Smart. Otherwise, the AI we built would be just like any other.
target: &105 很聪明。否则，我们造出的人工智能，也会跟其他的毫无分别。

source: &106 You must have made some powerful friends in Newton since you left Buenos Aires.
target: &106 离开布宜诺斯艾利斯后，你一定在牛顿市结交了不少有权势的朋友。

source: &107 I'm surprised they didn't just contract this AI project out to corporate research.
target: &107 他们居然没把这个人工智能项目直接外包给企业研究机构，我还挺惊讶。

source: &228 The fear then is dependence upon the private sector in all future matters.
target: &228 那样一来，今后所有事情都得依赖私营部门，这正是他们的顾虑。

source: &229 However, if we should not succeed, that will be their next option.
target: &229 不过，如果我们失败，他们下一步就会选择那条路。

source: &108 But...that's not going to happen, is it?
target: &108 但……我们不会失败，对吧？

source: &230 I am afraid that we have hit an obstacle.
target: &230 恐怕，我们遇到了一个障碍。

source: &231 Though we have a solid theoretical groundwork, we cannot proceed.
target: &231 虽然理论基础已经扎实，可我们没办法继续。

source: &109 Why not? We've built a gene-map for the organic processors.
target: &109 为什么？我们已经为有机处理器建立了基因图谱。

source: &110 Get Charlie or Dr Chigwa to run it through a flash-clone!
target: &110 让查理或者奇格瓦博士，用速成克隆体试一下！

source: &232 Alas, that is where our problem lies.
target: &232 唉，问题恰恰就在这里。

source: &233 Our plans depend upon the development of neural tissue.
target: &233 我们的计划依赖神经组织的发育。

source: &234 The flash-clones develop with none, for legal and ethical reasons.
target: &234 出于法律和伦理的原因，速成克隆体不会发育出神经组织。

source: &111 The city council must have expected something like this eventually.
target: &111 市议会迟早该料到会有这种情况。

source: &112 We can petition for a special exception, they'll provide live embryos for research...
target: &112 我们可以申请特批，请他们提供活胚胎用于研究……

source: &235 Certainly possible, though too lengthy.
target: &235 当然可以，但耗时太久。

source: &236 By the time approval has been granted, the project will have exceeded its deadline.
target: &236 等到获批，项目早就超过期限了。

source: &113 Dr Baxter has a reliable simulation of the AI running in situ.
target: &113 巴克斯特博士已经有一个可靠的人工智能模拟系统，在现场运行。

source: &114 Surely he can pattern it out into a larger system?
target: &114 他总能把它扩展到更大的系统里吧？

source: &237 While the platform will run magnificently in an organic framework...
target: &237 这个平台放在有机框架中，确实可以运行得十分出色……

source: &238 ...trying to emulate it in simulation has tremendous processing costs.
target: &238 ……可要用模拟方式实现它，就需要极其庞大的计算资源。

source: &239 Unless we can finalise the production of an organic matrix...we will fail.
target: &239 除非完成有机矩阵的生产……否则我们注定失败。

source: &115 There might be another option...Nina gave me the idea.
target: &115 也许还有别的办法……妮娜给了我一个主意。

source: &116 We need normal embryos to gengineer, not the flash-clones, right?
target: &116 我们需要普通胚胎来做基因工程，而不是速成克隆体，对吧？

source: &240 That is our problem. The council will not be able to provide them quickly enough.
target: &240 正是这个问题。议会来不及提供普通胚胎。

source: &117 Well...Charlie and I have been...trying for kids...
target: &117 嗯……查理和我一直在……尝试要孩子……

source: &118 As a result, we have several fertilized embryos frozen.
target: &118 所以，我们冷冻保存了几个受精胚胎。

source: &241 Viksha, I hope you are saying what I think!
target: &241 维克莎，希望你要说的正是我想的那件事！

source: &119 We could...perhaps...donate...
target: &119 我们可以……也许……捐出……

source: &242 You do not know what this could mean to us!
target: &242 你不知道，这对我们有多重要！

source: &243 You have SAVED us, Viksha.
target: &243 你救了我们，维克莎。

source: &244 In a way, you may yet be the surrogate mother of the Central AI.
target: &244 从某种意义上说，你也许会成为中枢人工智能的代孕母亲。

source: &35 Whoa, big spike in activity there...
target: &35 哇，活动突然大幅增强了……

source: &27 You think Charlie'll be okay with that?
target: &27 你觉得查理会同意吗？

source: &120 Hey, he's spent years modifying embryos himself.
target: &120 嘿，他自己也花了好几年改造胚胎。

source: &121 I'm sure he'll be alright...
target: &121 我相信，他不会介意……

source: &32 Sorry, Nina. I'm just not used to that name yet.
target: &32 抱歉，妮娜。我还不太习惯这个姓。

source: &10 Congratulations, by the way.
target: &10 顺便说一句，恭喜你。

source: &11 Isn't it kind of old fashioned though, taking his name?
target: &11 不过，随他的姓，是不是有点老派？

source: &33 You know Charlie. He's a traditional kind of guy.
target: &33 你也知道查理，他这个人挺传统的。

source: &12 Yeah, they sure don't make 'em like that anymore.
target: &12 是啊，现在可找不到几个那样的人了。

source: &34 He's definitely brought some of his homeland with him.
target: &34 他肯定把一些家乡的习惯也带来了。

source: &35 It wasn't that important to me, anyway.
target: &35 反正，对我来说，这也没那么重要。

source: &13 I guess families are still doing that in those parts.
target: &13 那边的家庭，大概还保留着这种习惯。

source: &14 Speaking of families, you guys planning on starting one?
target: &14 说到家庭，你们打算要孩子吗？

source: &36 I think it's romantic.
target: &36 我觉得挺浪漫的。

source: &15 Not a giant leap backwards?
target: &15 我看更像是倒退了一大步吧？

source: &37 He lost his family in the war, now we're starting a new one.
target: &37 他在战争中失去了家人，现在我们要建立一个新的家。

source: &38 I thought it might help give him some continuity.
target: &38 我想，这也许能让他感觉，自己的人生仍有延续。

source: &16 Speaking of which, you guys planning on having kids?
target: &16 说到这个，你们打算要孩子吗？

source: &39 Eventually, yes. We're speaking to a specialist.
target: &39 迟早会的。我们正在咨询专家。

source: &17 Oohh, right. Hotzone.
target: &17 哦，对。强辐射区。

source: &18 Who'd have thought living in a hazard region would be such a drag?
target: &18 谁想到，住在危险地区竟会这么麻烦呢？

source: &40 It's not just Charlie, my work with the Inspectors wasn't good for me either.
target: &40 不只是查理。我从前跟核查团一起工作，身体也受了影响。

source: &19 Going for the test-tube baby option, then?
target: &19 所以，打算做试管婴儿？

source: &41 It'll be a whole lot easier to screen for anything we might pass down.
target: &41 这样，就容易筛查出我们可能遗传给孩子的问题。

source: &20 With Charlie's background, I'm surprised he's not growing them himself.
target: &20 以查理的背景，我倒很惊讶，他没打算自己培育。

source: &41 Then again, they might go "bang" if he did it.
target: &41 不过，真让他培育，没准孩子会“砰”地一下。

source: &21 Too far?
target: &21 玩笑过头了？

source: &42 Yes.
&43 It's our only issue at the moment.
target: &43 这是我们现在唯一有分歧的事。

source: &44 Everything else, we agree on - except that.
target: &44 除了这个，其他事，我们的意见都一致。

source: &23 Everyone's got to have some kind of drama.
target: &23 谁都难免有点烦心事。

source: &24 Neither of you want to give up the career to become a full-time parent?
target: &24 你们谁都不愿意放弃事业，当全职父母？

source: &45 It's not that, it's just...our backgrounds.
target: &45 不是，只是……我们的经历。

source: &25 Ah - he's from a hotzone, isn't he?
target: &25 啊，他来自强辐射区，是吧？

source: &46 It isn't that I NEVER want kids...
target: &46 也不是说，我一辈子都不想要孩子……

source: &26 ...you'd just rather they came out with all the parts they're supposed to have.
target: &26 ……只是希望，孩子出生时，该有的部位都齐全。

source: &47 I guess you could say that.
target: &47 可以这么说。

source: &48 We're going to do it safely. We've got a specialist involved.
target: &48 我们会确保安全。已经请专家来帮忙了。

source: &16 Hi there.
&17 I'm Dr Perera.
target: &17 我是佩雷拉博士。

source: &1 Yes.
&18 I...uh...thought I might get to know who I'm going to be working with?
target: &18 我……呃……只是想认识一下，以后要一起工作的同事？

source: &2 Oh! Right, certainly. Adam Baxter.
target: &2 哦！对，当然。亚当·巴克斯特。

source: &19 You enjoying the...uh...MRI scanner?
target: &19 您很喜欢这台……呃……磁共振扫描仪？

source: &3 Ah, yes. Forgive me, it's just been some time since my last labwork.
target: &3 啊，是。请原谅，我已经很久没在实验室里工作了。

source: &4 After the...accident...no institution would take me.
target: &4 那场……事故之后……没有机构肯收留我。

source: &5 I feel as though I may wake up, and have this *dream* of an assignment taken from me.
target: &5 我总觉得，自己随时会醒来，这份梦寐以求的工作也就没了。

source: &20 Don't worry, Dr Vargas is an excellent judge of talent.
target: &20 别担心，瓦尔加斯博士很会识人。

source: &21 I can guarantee that this isn't merely out of pity.
target: &21 我可以保证，这绝不只是出于同情。

source: &6 This is something of a last chance for me.
target: &6 对我来说，这差不多是最后一次机会。

source: &7 We must succeed!
target: &7 我们必须成功！

source: &8 I hope you'll excuse me, I *must* ensure the MRI scanner is calibrated.
target: &8 抱歉失陪，我必须确保磁共振扫描仪校准妥当。

source: &9 ...not aligned...not aligned...why...mmrmrm...
target: &9 ……没对齐……没对齐……为什么……唔唔……

source: &22 Oof! Hello, Charlie!
target: &22 唔！你好，查理！

source: &23 What was that for?
target: &23 这是干什么？

source: &1 I'm not sure...I was...just worried you weren't gonna come.
target: &1 我也不知道……我只是……担心你不来了。

source: &24 Don't be silly, of course I was going to be here!
target: &24 别傻了，我当然会来！

source: &2 I know...I was just...afraid.
target: &2 我知道……我只是……害怕。

source: &25 Hey, there's no need to be afraid of anything, here.
target: &25 嘿，在这里没什么好怕的。

source: &26 Unlike your last job, there's no firing squad for motivation.
target: &26 这可不像你上一份工作，不会有行刑队逼你干活。

source: &27 I'm...sorry, I didn't mean...
target: &27 对……对不起，我不是想……

source: &3 It's hard to believe all that's behind me...
target: &3 很难相信，那些事都已经过去了……

source: &4 Not only do I have you to thank for getting me out of there...
target: &4 我不只得谢谢你把我从那里救出来……

source: &6 ...but getting me into this role, as well!
target: &6 ……还得谢谢你，帮我找到这份工作！

source: &28 All I did was mention you to Dr Vargas.
target: &28 我只是跟瓦尔加斯博士提了提你。

source: &29 He knew what he needed, and you fit the bill.
target: &29 他知道自己需要什么，而你正好符合。

source: &30 Obviously he knows talent when he sees it.
target: &30 显然，他识得出人才。

source: &7 Hopefully he likes my work.
target: &7 希望他喜欢我的工作。

source: &8 He can't exactly go to the Texan warlords for a reference.
target: &8 总不能指望他找得克萨斯的军阀给我写推荐信。

source: &31 That's a good sign - now you're the one making jokes about it!
target: &31 好兆头，现在换你拿这事开玩笑了！

source: &9 This is impressive equipment they've got.
target: &9 他们这里的设备真是厉害。

source: &10 I wonder what we're all here for...
target: &10 不知道把我们都找来，是为了什么……

source: &16 The uptake reports came in.
target: &16 新基因的整合报告出来了。

source: &17 Looks like there was a 99.1% volume of new code in the embryo.
target: &17 看起来，胚胎中新编码的整合比例达到了99.1%。

source: &49 That's fantastic! We'll have a viable specimen for testing within days!
target: &49 太棒了！再过几天，我们就能得到可供测试的存活样本！

source: &18 Yeah, and it wouldn't have had the same kind of uptake if it was one of the braindead ones.
target: &18 是啊，要是用那种没有大脑的胚胎，整合效果可不会这么好。

source: &19 So, how did you manage to score these full-scope human embryos?
target: &19 所以，你是怎么弄到这些具备完整发育能力的人类胚胎的？

source: &50 It would have taken months to get approval from the city council.
target: &50 等市议会审批，得等上好几个月。

source: &51 So...we used our own.
target: &51 所以……我们用了自己的。

source: &20 Yours...you and Charlie?
target: &20 你们的……你和查理的？

source: &52 They're healthy, and they've got all the right uptake markers.
target: &52 它们很健康，也有所有适合基因整合的标记。

source: &21 Oh, I'm just kinda surprised Charlie agreed to it.
target: &21 哦，查理居然同意了，我只是有点惊讶。

source: &22 Given his previous line of work, and all...
target: &22 毕竟他以前做过那种工作……

source: &23 You *have* told him, haven't you?
target: &23 你*已经*告诉他了，对吧？

source: &54 I was...going to find a way...
target: &54 我本来……打算找个合适的机会……

source: &24 That explains why he's on the warpath, then.
target: &24 难怪他气势汹汹的。

source: &55 Oh, nuke me...how did he find out?
target: &55 哦，炸死我算了……他怎么知道的？

source: &11 VICKY!!!
&25 Uh-oh.
&12 Dr Chigwa, may I speak to my wife?
target: &12 奇格瓦博士，能让我跟我妻子单独谈谈吗？

source: &26 Charlie, you'd better not -
target: &26 查理，你最好别——

source: &13 Get OUT!!!
&14 Dr Baxter just congratulated me on what a noble gesture I was making for science.
target: &14 巴克斯特博士刚才还在恭喜我，说我为了科学作出了多么高尚的奉献。

source: &15 Apparently, "we" volunteered our own embryos for gengineering.
target: &15 据说，“我们”自愿拿出自己的胚胎，供基因工程实验使用。

source: &56 You don't need to worry about it, it's all legal.
target: &56 你不用担心，这全是合法的。

source: &57 Not like we've used an organ-legger; they've been sourced legitimately.
target: &57 我们又没找器官贩子，来源完全正当。

source: &28 Uh-huh. You used your own, didn't you?
target: &28 嗯哼。你用的是自己的，对不对？

source: &58 Um - how did you find out?
target: &58 呃……你怎么知道的？

source: &29 Same way Charlie did.
target: &29 跟查理一样。

source: &59 Oh, nuke me...he knows?
target: &59 哦，炸死我算了……他知道了？

source: &30 He's been on the warpath looking for you all evening.
target: &30 他整个晚上都怒气冲冲地在找你。

source: &60 Charlie, calm down.
target: &60 查理，冷静点。

source: &61 You're making too big a deal out of this!
target: &61 你把这事看得太严重了！

source: &16 You think I'm overreacting?!
target: &16 你觉得我反应过度？！

source: &17 You have NO idea what I'm upset about!
target: &17 你根本不知道我为什么生气！

source: &62 Sure I do...
target: &62 我当然知道……

source: &63 I'm sorry I hadn't told you yet - Dr Vargas is having enough trouble stalling the council.
target: &63 对不起，我还没告诉你。瓦尔加斯博士光是拖住议会就已经够吃力了。

source: &64 We needed to start showing results, so I made the decision for both of us.
target: &64 我们必须拿出成果，所以我替我们两个人作了决定。

source: &18 You didn't think I'd object if I knew beforehand?
target: &18 你就没想过，要是提前知道，我会反对？

source: &65 Well, no - using our own embryos was the right thing to do to keep the project afloat.
target: &65 没有。为了让项目继续下去，用我们自己的胚胎才是正确的选择。

source: &36 You have NO idea what I'm upset about!
target: &36 你根本不知道我为什么生气！

source: &66 You're mad because I didn't talk with you about it first.
target: &66 你生气，是因为我没有先跟你商量。

source: &19 No! Well, yes I am, but that's not why I feel like this.
target: &19 不是！好吧，我是生气，可这不是我这么难受的原因。

source: &67 I understand, it was a big decision - we've invested a lot of time and energy into having kids.
target: &67 我明白，这是个重大的决定。为了要孩子，我们花了那么多时间和精力。

source: &68 I'd probably be upset in your position, but I'd have hoped you'd trust me to make choices for the both of us.
target: &68 换成我，我可能也会生气，但我希望你能信任我，让我为我们俩作决定。

source: &20 Oh God, you haven't understood what's wrong with this at all!
target: &20 天哪，你根本没明白这件事错在哪里！

source: &69 Y'know, sometimes your old-world sensibilities are charming - but not this time.
target: &69 你知道，你那些旧时代的观念有时还挺可爱，但这次不行。

source: &70 What is it they believe where you're from, that "life begins at conception"?
target: &70 你老家的人信什么来着，“生命始于受孕”？

source: &21 You know damn well what I've done with human gengineering in the past.
target: &21 我以前用人类基因工程干过什么，你清楚得很。

source: &22 I'm well past being able to object for moral reasons.
target: &22 我早就没资格拿道德理由来反对了。

source: &71 We're only using one, maybe two of the embryos we've got for the project.
target: &71 我们只打算拿一个，也许两个胚胎用于这个项目。

source: &72 The other four are still stored at Al-Rasis.
target: &72 另外四个还保存在阿尔拉西斯。

source: &23 It's not a matter of whether we can make more or not!
target: &23 这跟我们还能不能再弄出更多胚胎没有关系！

source: &24 We could have THOUSANDS of embryos on standby, it'd still be wrong!
target: &24 就算我们有几千个备用胚胎，这样做也还是错的！

source: &73 It's not as if we're bringing the embryos to term.
target: &73 我们又没打算让这些胚胎发育到出生。

source: &74 Their lives aren't going to be affected by the alterations we're making!
target: &74 我们所作的改造，不会影响它们以后的人生！

source: &25 We've ALREADY affected them by USING them in this role!
target: &25 拿它们来干这种事，就已经影响了它们！

source: &75 Have you seen the uptake results Dr Chigwa recorded?
target: &75 你看过奇格瓦博士记录的基因整合结果吗？

source: &76 We've got over 95% success, the neural tissue-development is going to be phenomenal!
target: &76 成功率超过95%，神经组织的发育效果会非常出色！

source: &26 I don't give a damn about the results!
target: &26 我根本不在乎什么结果！

source: &77 It's not the fact that we're engineering human embryos...
target: &77 问题不在于我们改造的是人类胚胎……

source: &78 ...it's that they're OUR embryos.
target: &78 ……而在于，那是我们自己的胚胎。

source: &27 I spent two years, WEAPONIZING children...
target: &27 我花了两年时间，把孩子变成武器……

source: &28 The fact that they were destined...*doomed* to a purpose...
target: &28 他们注定……*逃不掉*那个为他们安排好的用途……

source: &79 It's one thing to have your life affected by a quirk of genetics,
target: &79 因为基因的偶然差异而影响人生，是一回事，

source: &80 ...but when you've been deliberately altered before birth to fit a role...
target: &80 ……可要是为了某种用途，在出生前就被人刻意改造……

source: &29 I'd hoped that I'd escaped it, but...seeing it with our own kids, it's just...
target: &29 我以为自己已经逃离了那些事，可是……看见同样的事发生在我们自己的孩子身上，我实在……

source: &81 I...understand, Charlie. I'll talk to Dr Vargas about it.
target: &81 我……明白了，查理。我会跟瓦尔加斯博士谈谈。

source: &30 He won't be happy - it sounds like he was counting on this.
target: &30 他不会高兴的。听起来，他就指望这个了。

source: &82 He'll just have to deal with it.
target: &82 那也只能让他自己接受了。

source: &1 Hello! I'm James, and I'm the one responsible for making this game.
&2 You've enabled the developer commentary, and since I'm the developer, I'm darn well going to comment on things.
&3 Just click the "comment" icons for more background information wherever you are.
&4 Or I might just butt in if I think I've got something interesting and handsome to say.
&5 Have fun, and see you in the future!
&6 When people hear the word "cyberspace", that immediately conjures up certain mental images.
&7 I wanted to make sure that the Trance was evocative of this, especially if you grew up in the 80s/90s.
&8 We also wanted to make the art distinctly different from the "real world" scenes in the game.
&9 All of the Trance bits are done in Ben's more conventional art style, without the speech portraits.
&10 I started making Technobabylon in 2010, when I was working as an English Teacher in South Korea.
&11 Latha's room is, in fact, based on the apartment I'd been assigned to live in.
&12 Things like the drain in the floor to make it easier to just hose off the apartment, and all the piles of clothes.
&13 Plus, those sentient food machines they've got over there. What a country!
&14 This version of the room was the first scene that Ben Chandler did for the game.
&15 I knew immediately that he absolutely *got* the atmosphere we were aiming for.
&16 Because I'm quite unsubtle, I like to draw parallels between this future, and lots of classical references.
&17 This garden, high up on the side of a tower, is supposed to be evocative of images of the Hanging Gardens of Babylon...
&18 ...of Techno-Babylon...you see?
&19 Plus, if your futuristic megacity's floorspace is taken up with roads and buildings, where else are people going to have gardens?
&20 When I started making this game, I had just discovered parallax, the illusion of background objects moving more slowly to simulate distance.
&21 Once you know it's a thing, you start to see it *everywhere* in animation, because it's so versatile.
&22 I just HAD to make a scene out of it, hence this highway.
&23 When Janet Gilbert saw it, her first reaction was "This is going to *murder* the iPhone version."
&24 This scene has gotten a lot busier since its first iteration.
&25 That floaty robot, the flashing cones, all these things were added when Ben was tasked with making scenes more...vibrant.
&26 This is another example of me basing things on my time in Korea - the station's based off a train station in Seoul I remember.
&27 It's amazing, they don't even have ticket barriers or anything!
&28 Of course, I always paid. I have scruples.
&29 This part of the game came into being when I was spending a lot of time in Paris with my wife on business.
&30 Well, *she* was on business. I was just sponging off her Eurostar points.
&31 This is pretty much the view from our hotel room.
&32 Even in itself, La Defense probably the most cyberpunk part of Paris I've seen - or corporate, at least. Glass skyscrapers everywhere.
&33 It's like if William Gibson wrote things with more croissants.
&34 Despite this being the second chapter of the game, this part of it was added last, funnily enough.
&35 Waving his sceptre of executive meddling, Dave (Gilbert) decided that the pacing wasn't quite right the way it was before.
&36 Anyone who played the old version of Technobabylon will notice that this wasn't here, after all.
&37 However, we adapted, and ended up with a bit that, I think, better sets up the whole "investigation" thing.
&38 This being a Wadjet Eye game, we needed more offices as scenes as well.
&39 We were way below our "office" quotient, and management was starting to get uncomfortable.
&40 Thanks to this scene, Technobabylon now has 33% more offices than originally planned for.
&41 While a lot of the city is quite dirty, as you might have seen, we wanted CEL to be the opposite.
&42 In a way, a location's cleanliness is representative of just how much care it's given by its occupants, and by Central.
&43 So CEL, right under its very nose, is always spick-and-span, with its army of robot custodial staff.
&44 While it looks cold, and decorated by an emotionless machine, I think it'd the kind of style I'd give *my* workplace. Except for all the cameras.
&45 If this were an RPG, this would be where you decide whether to use your skills in lockpicking, or just smash down the door.
&46 I look forward to seeing, when this game comes out, which option most people use to get through it.
&47 Mmm, all this thought of kitchens is making me hungry.
&48 My wife is making apple pie downstairs too, so the smell isn't helping.
&49 This is one of the scenes that was *not* built using a 3D model for references.
&50 No matter how many times I fiddled the model, I couldn't get something that looked right.
&51 As a result, I left it to Ben's expertise, and we got this delightful outcome.
&52 The only thing that needed alteration was the level of...decoration.
&53 I think I had to ask for MORE GORE a couple of times. After all, there's a lot of fluid in a man of Giel's size.
&54 A big thank-you to Ashton Raze, whose spine we borrowed for the image on the screens.
&55 X-Raze, if you will.
&56 CEL was one of those situations where you come up with the acronym first, then figure out what it stands for later.
&57 In this case, "Centralized Emergency Logistics." CEL handles public security, firefighting and rescue for the city.
&58 Have you tried making calls on the computer terminal, yet?
&59 In the end, we have 102 different responses, and I want to give a big thanks to everyone who contributed.
&60 Some people have thought that the tone of the calls might not be right for dark cyberpunk,
&61 ...but there's plenty of humour to be found in real-life, no matter how grim your situation is.
&62 Besides, it struck me as the BRITISH thing to do.
&63 In the old and preview versions, this is where part 2 ends. Now, it's the end of 3.
&64 We had to do some rejigging for flow and timing, what with all the extra bits being added in.
&65 Here in Newton, these apartments aren't designed to be *terrible* - they've got everything you need, after all.
&66 Ironically, my plan had started off with the city being a much more "ideal" place to live.
&67 After all, the state provides basic housing, clothing, food and a net connection. What more could you need?
&68 Like a disturbing amount of what I make, this room is based on something I saw in a dream.
&69 Does it count as working overtime if you do your planning while you're asleep?
&70 A recurring theme for Latha - having to escape from a room.
&71 Fortunately, with the Trance, she has more than just the physical world to fool around in.
&72 This is the kind of scene that really benefits from Ben's own style.
&73 What with the upcoming Shardlight (Wadjet Eye Games, 2015) it's obvious that dystopia is his thing.
&74 Sometimes you might see writing in Chinese/Japanese, a staple of good cyberpunk.
&75 Unfortunately, my Mandarin is somewhat non-existent, so I have to take Ben's word that none of it's obscene.
&76 Back in 2011, when I was first planning this stage, I wanted to make the Trance 3D, and the adventure bits retro-style.
&77 A kind of irony - that the "virtual" would have more realism than the "real" in a sense.
&78 I managed to get a kind of working system in AGS with a 3D plugin, but then the changeover to AGS3.0 happened.
&79 Perhaps in the future, I'll try something similar. Like when I've got an Oculus Rift, or something.
&80 This is Jinsil's first appearance, and in the older versions, the only one.
&81 It was only when I got around to the full game that I settled on the "arabian" theme to their avatar.
&82 Although "Jinsil" is a Korean word, since this was designed as a clue to their identity later on.
&84 I think this is one of my favorite parts of the game, atmosphere-wise.
&85 Nathan did a fantastic job with the music, excatly got what I meant by "almost tropical".
&86 I am both disturbed and excited by the implications of being able to create new organisms at the genetic level from scratch.
&87 When that procedure becomes routine, it basically becomes a factory line.
&88 Even today, companies are patenting living things. Does that cheapen life?
&89 Is it somehow perverse if we take something nature's been perfecting for millions of years, and do it more efficiently ourselves?
&90 I'm certainly not equipped to answer that, but asking those kinds of questions is what sci-fi is for.
&91 /pretentious author mode: OFFLINE
&92 Anyone who's seen the movie "Sunshine" might feel a few notes of familiarity in this room.
&93 If you haven't, then go and see Sunshine. It's a brilliant movie.
&94 I'm not allowed to use the word "classic" to describe movies anymore. My wife tells me I overdo it.
&95 Now she charges me a quid every time I do it.
&96 Is there anything quite as sci-fi as an airlock?
&97 It's a sign of "SERIOUS BUSINESS HERE", and it can go anywhere from space, to labs.
&98 When I was a boy, I used to want an airlock on my bedroom door.
&99 Not because I was particularly ecohazardous or anything, just because they were SO COOL.
&100 My brother on the other hand - phew, talk about deadly release of toxic gases!
&101 When I worked as a taxman in a previous life, I got to see an enormous storage warehouse where paper records were kept.
&102 24 hours a day, robots would shoot along rails, up, down, side-to-side, opening and closing drawers.
&103 This is another example of "we're already living in the future".
&104 If you look out of the window, Lao remarks that she can almost see all the way to Mombasa.
&105 It's interesting to note where people believe the city of Newton to be, in this world.
&106 A lot of people assume North America, some say Europe, but it's intentionally vague and cosmopolitan as an independent city-state.
&107 If you pay attention to the clues (like the newspapers), you'll learn that the city is almost equatorial, in East Africa.
&108 Just a little bit up the coast from Mombasa, in what would today be Somalia.
&109 Partly because the equator's a good place for space launches/elevators, and also symbology.
&110 After all, around there, you've got some of the earliest examples of human civilization.
&111 Plus, I was born in Nairobi.
&112 I. Love. Parallax. Seriously, these stairs, dude.
&113 Took a bit of engineering, and a heck of a lot of trickery, but they were made to work eventually.
&114 If anyone can ruin a city, it's Ben Chandler - in the most positive sense possible.
&115 He knows how to make it look like the place has been abandoned for years, and abused by 'artists' ever since.
&116 Of course, with Ben's backgrounds, you have to look for hidden meanings in the graffiti.
&117 DYNAMIC ENTRY!!!
&118 Dave Gilbert's definitely been a real trooper, taking on so many of the voices himself.
&119 All of the strike team are him, after being modulated a bit.
&120 Nah, I'm not saying anything until the strike team gets here.
&121 I needed to find an excuse for a large water supply to be so close to the laser's electricity.
&122 Hence, why the shower is up here. I'm sure they've got showers in factories, really.
&123 Probably.
&124 I had originally envisaged a much more complex puzzle involving changing the laser's path in real-time while it was on.
&125 Then I tried working out how to make it work in AGS, went insane, and had to be committed for the sake of public safety.
&126 So, in the end, we opted for rotating the arm around outside.
&127 This abandoned factory was one of the bits of the game I'd had planned from the get-go.
&128 This part of the city was abandoned after a geomagnetic anomaly, like the Carrington Event in 1859.
&129 Seriously, read up on it. It's bloomin' terrifying, if that kind of thing happened these days.
&130 *My* career would certainly take a nosedive.
&131 Adventure games tend to be...slower. Some of our testers were having difficulty staying behind the large objects.
&132 That's fair enough - reflex puzzles aren't for everyone, and I'm no lover of "press Z to not die" situations.
&133 So, every time Regis is killed, the 'safe zone' behind the big objects gets wider and wider.
&134 Fail enough times, and you can just walk across. The guard will just ignore you.
&135 You'd have to do pretty spectacularly badly to achieve that, though.
&136 I have nothing against Singapore. Really. It's a lovely place, I just needed an Asian city whose name started with 'S'.
&137 Continuing with the game's theme of people taking things waaaay too far, I thought I'd push it with atomic war.
&138 These guys are obsessed with it, like someone today might be about trains, or military paraphenalia.
&139 But, it becomes a bit more disturbing in a world where they've already had a few nuclear conflicts.
&140 It's why everyone uses 'nuke' as the curse-word of choice. Atomic warfare is a sensitive topic to a lot of people here.
&141 I've said it before, and I'll say it again, Ben Chandler is *great* at this kind of scenery.
&142 I'd send him a greyscale 3D model, and he'd turn it into...this!
&143 Though plenty of the city is nice and shiny, many areas are run-down and dilapidated.
&144 Personally, I think a city's cleanliness and upkeep is a reflection of the feelings and mental health of its residents.
&145 In this case, everyone's so preoccupied with their own virtual worlds, they just let the real one crumble around them.
&146 Have you ever seen the movie, Blade Runner? You might have guessed, it's one of my favourites. A classic.
&147 I'm of the opinion that Deckard *was* a replicant.
&148 More unsubtle linking of heavy substance abuse, and dependence upon the virtual.
&149 Don't get me wrong, I've nothing against the idea of the Trance. Heck, I'd love something like that.
&150 But addiction, and too much of anything can be a problem.
&151 Also, another appearance by the delightful Ashton Raze.
&152 Given the time, resources, and ability to outsource, I would love to do SO MUCH more with the Trance.
&153 But, by working it as a 'closed' server here, it allowed us to keep focus.
&154 Again, the users of the Trance are going for the 'post-retro' cyberspace aesthetic.
&155 Lots of MMO games have 'bar' scenes, especially RPGs.
&156 This establishment is here because:
&157 a) I needed a way for the player to get their hands on deadly acids.
&158 and b) I wanted to use the bartender again.
&159 Couldn't *quite* justify reusing Cheffie the Chef here, though.
&160 The more things change, the more things stay the same.
&161 I've no doubt people will still be playing the intellectual descendents of tennis and Pong by the 2080s.
&162 Except by then, it'll be a 'classical' thing.
&163 Ugh, it gives me the shivers, thinking of computer games being over a century old by this stage.
&164 Granted, I'll be exactly 100 years old on this day - I set the game on my birthday.
&165 The idea for this place came up in a philosophical debate I had at university.
&166 It started with "is synthetic meat ethically sound for vegetarians?"
&167 After all, if it's just muscle tissue grown in a vat, and no animals have suffered for its creation, what's wrong with it?
&168 While that got some nods, the argument was then extended to: "What if it were human muscle tissue?"
&169 That seemed to complicate the matter a little. I can see it as the kind of thing wealthy celebrities would do, though.
&170 The kind of people who'd then have the mindset of "well, why do people want to eat him, but not *ME*?"
&171 Get them marketing their own cuts of themselves.
&172 This is just human nature. You don't even need to look into the future for this sort of thing.
&173 In a future of automated food machines, there will always be *some* people who want their dining done the old-fashioned way.
&174 Kind of like how one goes to the theatre these days, despite TV and the internet.
&175 In some games, to avoid having to worry about real-time reflections in mirrors, just use a dull, slightly shiny surface.
&176 In this case, I've gone for the option of the over-complicated mirror of the future.

&2 I'll be joining you through the commentary to talk about some of the ideas, some of the techniques and some of the processes behind the art...
&3 Which hopefully will be interesting, funny or will help you achieve everything you wanted to achieve in life, love and workplace. Enjoy!
&10 The very first scene we see Latha in is her suspended in the flow of data, and here I wanted to make a subtle reference to the Vitruvian Man image by Leonardo Da Vinci.
&11 Because to me it represents a convergence between mathmatics and mankind, which I think most people have seen, and I think that represents Latha's character very well.
&12 The data numbers falling in cascade is obviously a reference to the film 'The Matrix', whose aesthetic I remain very fond of. And I think it's a reference most people will get.
&13 For most of the scenes in the game, James would give me a basic 3D skeleton that he'd done in Blender of where he wanted things in the room to go.
&14 And onto these I'd lay the human touches - the color, the texture, the decoration, the dirt, the grime. You know...all the human little touches.

&15 So you can see here the rotating discs beneath the floor, which James created, and I put these into my Photoshop file frame by frame, and mixed them frame by frame with things like the glittering data in the air...
&16 And then exported them manually one by one. Which was a fairly painstaking process, but I think worth it for the sort of things that we could achieve with this.

&20 I love Deus Ex, and I know James is the same, so the colors chosen for this, which is the very first scene I drew for the game, are the orange and blue which are both sides of the Deus Ex art style.
&21 I actually drew this before James could give me any direction. I'd played the freeware stuff and I knew how the room looked...

&22 When James and I agreed that we were going to work together, I jumped right in and did this before he had a chance to tell me anything that he wanted. So he was actually going to change the design of this room from the earlier version.
&23 So sorry to James for being so hasty. But I think it ended up all right!
&30 I had actually finished my work on Technobabylon when James and Dave decided that one part needed to be cut, and this part needed to be added.
&31 At first Dave and I discussed it and he wanted to have the person bouncing off the car and landing on the street, but I thought that was too exaggerated.
&32 But then I thought that often something happens in animation - especially when you don't have the ability to frame the shot as you do in films...
&33 When it's something subtle, you actually miss it, and it only hits you after it has happened.
&34 So I think giving the guy some hang time (as I eventually ended up doing) and some time to bleed out gives the player some time to process what's actually happening.
&40 When James first gave me the moving skeleton of this scene for me to add color/texture/lights to, I was pretty nervous about how it would look in-game.
&41 I'd never done driving before. It always looked like a fairly complex thing to pull off well. And I'd imagined that if I DID do it, I'd use a side-on view for it.
&42 After adding all the details to the skeleton James gave me, and then doing the two backdrop layers that scroll in parallax, and then testing it all, I was surprised at how effective it is.
&43 It was a fair bit of work to do for what is effectively a location hub, but I really love how it ties the locations together and gives that feeling of travelling through a city.
&50 This is probably my favorite scene in the game. I love how the colors work together, and I managed to get a balance I really like - which isn't that common!
&51 The X-ray of the spine and chest was kindly donated to me by the lovely Nina White, and the X-ray of the wrist is one of my own wrist that I keep hanging on the wall.
&52 You never know when you're going to need an image of your own skeleton, somewhere.
&60 It's weird how sometimes the simplest scenes end up being the most effective visually. Sometimes the more complex a scene is (while more decorative) the more cluttered it ends up being.

&61 And so the more open/clean ones like this present a more readable/pleasant composition to our eyes which is important for indicating to players where they should go, what they should click on, and where they can walk.
&62 I think James's idea of having the desks set at an angle to us also helps give this a more natural, human look.
&63 The straight, rectangular look of a desk that faces us is a really artificial looking thing and having an angle like this really breaks that up.
&70 It's interesting how the smallest elements can make a scene feel more authentic. I didn't much care for this scene for most of the production. It felt a little average to me.

&71 But when it came time to do the background animations after all the important stuff had been finished, I created a couple of glowing light top cones and a floating security drone. And somehow these really gave the scene what I think they need.
&72 A bit of motion in a backdrop in a scene can really change the whole feel of it. It really brings it to life.
&73 Especially in the case of, like, a police scene - having the flashing lights and everything - is really indicative of authority. It's what we are used to seeing.
&74 I think that's definitely the case here. It took a scene that I didn't like much and gave it the atmosphere that I think it really needed to sell the idea.
&80 People sometimes ask me what the method I use for creating backgrounds, what the process is. And I say to them that the process varies quite a lot depending on the scene itself.
&81 In this particular scene, James had trouble getting the composition that he wanted in the basic 3D form. So I called him up on Skype, shared my screen, and sketched that freehand for him.
&82 This also resulted in a much looser sense of perspective and foreshortening then the very tight 3D ones that the rest of the game has in the non-Trance locations.
&83 Working on Technobabylon I have tightened my perspective up a lot. So you've probably got James to thank for that.
&90 I love dynamics. I love having something surprising in the middle of an otherwise, sort-of, predictable environment.
&91 And having this really organic area in the middle of such a very flat, manmade sort of world... the greens, the browns, the plant shapes. I really love that.
&92 I just gave James the mister drones and the pop-up mister, and I said you can use this wherever you want as many times you want. Wherever you want amongst the little plants.

&93 And I really love the order he gave it. It really gives the scene a bit of character, I think. So that's an animation I did just as a throwaway thing, I think it became the highlight of the scene for me.
&100 I actually really struggled getting this scene to a point where I was happy with it. For some reason the elements didn't come together very well for me.
&101 But adding the foreground plants somehow really made the scene for me.

&102 I'm not sure what it is about them that I like so much, but I think they break up what is otherwise a very 3D looking scene. It looks very artificial to me. Adding those in saved it for me personally.
&103 I'm not sure if anybody else thinks that, but it's nice for me to be able to look at it and go "Yeah that's done it. That's done the job."

&110 I actually though it was a little bit much to have two seperate scenes for a single location split up by a parallax foreground layer, but when I saw the final thing working I thought that James is a clever fellow.

&111 It does mean that you have to do to seperate scenes for the location, but I really like how the effect worked out. And blocking off the transition with that foreground layer was a very clever idea. So good thinking, James.
&112 I also only only did one spinning fan animation, and James just reused it a lot. So I can't complain that it was too much work. Because I cheated.
&120 My friend Ivan Ulyanov - great guy, great artist - he did the portraits that you are seeing in this game. Including this one you're seeing right now of my face.
&121 He recommended to me that I read a comic series called Transmetropolitan as a cyberpunk influence. And I adored Transmetropolitan. It was a great read.

&122 I really, really love Spider Jerusalem as a character. So in this little scene, as a little tribute to both Ivan and the comic series, I put in the three eyed smiley face and also a little spider above it.

&130 It's kind of funny. This location - just like the driving scene - is really just a location hub. There's not much to do. There's one guy to get past. And somehow it became one of the most elaborate things to construct in the game.
&131 I think I might have gotten a little bit carried away from what James's original vision was, but I really love the way it turned out.
&140 If you look over to the right, you'll see some letters stencilled on the machinery. Which those of you who have played another Wadjet Eye Game (Primordia) might recognize.
&141 I really love Vic's artwork in that game. Vic's a really nice guy and I really like talking to him and I wanted to make a reference to that game in here somewhere. So that's where I did it.
&150 I love graffiti in game locations. I think it adds a really human touch to what can otherwise look like what some man or lady sitting at a desk has just drawn. Which is what it is.
&151 A friend of mine, Sebastian, once told me that graffiti is there for a reason. People just want to express themselves for a reason, or they want to make their presense known.
&160 When James told me he wanted to have this guy have a virus put him in a prison inside his own mind, I wasn't really sure what to do.
&161 But I like Doom. And I like how Doom uses nice panoramic photos as a backdrop for Hell. So I thought, why don't I get a nice photo of a nice sky and turn it into this horrible red color.
&162 So you have Doom to thank for the way this turned out.
&170 When you think of cyberpunk you always think of the dark, neon-soaked streets of a grimy city. And it wasn't until this point in the game that we actually ended up doing that sort of scene.

&180 James had this idea that he wanted cyberspace should look very different from the real world. I wanted all the characters to have a kind of different style. Much like peoples' avatars on online forums, etc.

&181 And I did different styles for as many of the different characters as I could, and also tried to make none of them look like real world characters. I wanted everybody to be their own sort of person.
&182 So that explains the kind of incongruous styles here. I'm not sure it really carries over well to the final product, but that's the message and the feel that we were going to go for.
&183 Also, Dave Gilbert constantly threatens that he's going to make me animate a dance scene in a game, and it was James that ended up making me animate dancing.
&184 So Dave, you've been beaten to the dancing punch. I'm sorry.

&190 I love this area for a bunch of different reasons. Firstly because it allowed me to draw a lovely seascape vista with nice pink colors that is unlike any other location, any other place in this game.
&191 Secondly, because I was then allowed to blow it to smithereens, which is always fun! And doing a nuclear explosion isn't something I'd ever thought I'd animate in a game, but there we go.

&192 And thirdly because I got to draw a character whose avatar looks like a cross between a Fallout fanboy and a Full Throttle fanboy. Both of those are games which I adore. And to combine them into one weird and silly character was fantastic.
&200 Usually when drawing cityscapes for Technobabylon, I focused on a really blue palette for a really cold electronic feel. Even in areas where it's a little bit greener, I still stuck with it.

&201 But in this location, I didn't feel that the blue tone - the coldness of it - suited an exclusive restaurant where all these top people would come to meet. So I really warmed the color up as you can see in this skyscape.

&210 When James first told me that I was going to be drawing a room full of corposes I had really vivid, bold images of human beings hanging from meathooks and closeups and ribs sticking out and things.
&211 But actually when he showed me the final design, it was really a lot more polite than I was expecting. I'm not disappointed. It probably turned out for the best that we didn't get gratuitous.

&220 A nice thing about doing science fiction or invented, sort of, vehicles and locations, is that even in places where you've got boring areas, like  this simple hallway, you can add a lot of details.
&221 They're only visual noise, but they help break up the flat planes and make a, sort of, more textured thing that make it a lot more interesting.
&230 Ben Chandler (Art & Animation)
&240 One thing I try to avoid if I animate shimmering water on the ceiling or rippling water, as I have done both here, is try to avoid making it look like it's just been pasted onto the scene.
&241 So what I actually do is render both of them outside of photoshop, then paste it into photoshop, and then use adjustment/overlay layers  to make the whole scene feel more cohesive.
&242 It can be quite easy to have water effects stand out badly and look like cheap 90s effects. I'm not sure if I managed to avoided that here, but I've done my utmost!
&1 Greetings! I'm Nathan Allen Pinard and I'm responsible for creating the Music for this game.
&2 I'm also responsible for Sound Design, and some pretty cool vocal effects heard throughout the game.
&3 For the audiophiles out there that are interested in what I use, my main Digital Audio Workstation software is Studio One Pro 2.
&4 I also use several virtual instrument libraries like Hollywood Strings, Omnisphere, CineBrass CORE, Emotional Piano,
&5 Oracle, Project Alpha, Project Bravo, and some others I can't recall at the moment, but quite a few.
&6 I wasn't fully aware of what Trance music should sound like. I can partially understand Latha because she has a great deal of anxiety.
&7 Anxiety in the real world as opposed to trance. Kind of a hard-core form of social anxiety.
&8 I have anxiety myself, so I could relate to it. I sometimes avoid going out as the anxiety gets the best of me.
&9 So I simply asked James if Latha was meant to feel very good while in the Trance.
&10 The answer was yes, so I reflected that blissful feeling with the sort of computery digital feeling in the music. And this is the result.
&11 This ended up being the theme to the entire game as well.
&12 This is the first track I wrote for Technobabylon. I was told that the music in this scene should reflect that "something isn't quite right".
&13 However, it wasn't meant to be obvious what would happen, just that unsettling feeling.
&14 Knowing the character of Latha now though, this entire scene was meant to just show the anxiety she is feeling being in "meatspace".
&15 Using dissonance with muted strings is a useful tactic to show a scene that is tense, but not directly dangerous or exciting. Rather pretty actually.
&16 And I suppose I got that idea from a few iconic composers, such as Jerry Goldsmith, or Bernard Herrmann.
&17 Using wetware in technobabylon is such an important sound design moment, it's used so much, and it's the direct basis of integrating into tech.
&18 In a point-and-click, you generally don't have direct animations for everything. In this case you only see Latha touch something.
&19 This indicates one thing. That she's using wetware with something.
&20 So since there is no animation for that, we use sound design to show what happens.
&21 I literally had a picture of what it looked like. You can almost hear it.
&22 Something organic and gelatinous creeps into the tech you are connecting to, it connects digitally.
&23 And eventually you even hear a UI sound confirming you are connected.
&24 When I got the original VO for Cheffie, it was Jessica Pepper's normal voice. So naturally I had to alter her somehow.
&25 I added a few effects to her, the trance effect, a chorus, and a few other effects.
&26 But what's curious about this voice over, is she actually sang "T.H.E. Foods" in the original audio.
&27 So I imagined in a futuristic world like Technobabylon, that it would be heavily corporate.
&28 So I decided to use her singing as more of a jingle, or some kind of branding, while also including a synth behind her everytime she says it.
&29 I used Melodyne to have her sing the same notes every time, kind of like the NBC thing on TV.
&30 And that just turned out brilliant.
&31 This one was fun. In fact this whole scene was fun. Having to do sound design of a body hitting a car from a building is definitely a challenge.
&32 The scream was a random experiment. I had several friends in the room when inputting that just for fun.
&33 It made them spit their drinks out, so I knew it needed to stay. Having a bit of comedy in an otherwise dark scene, can be pretty useful.
&34 Of course I provided a non-comedy version and a comedy version to James, and naturally...he picked the comedy one.
&35 This entire scene to me, is a bit of a neat placement of various music cues.
&36 There are a number of tracks here that play into each other, that continue as if it's a fully scored timed scene that is static.
&37 You enter the room, the first scene music plays. Then it stops if you wait long enough.
&38 Then to go to the elevator, the body falls, track of suspense plays. That continues and runs out as well if you let it.
&39 Then the scroll up to the office happens, and new music there plays and at this point loops.
&40 If you click through dialogue or rush the scene, the music crossfades anyway, and it's like it was INTENDED.
&41 It ends up working almost like a TV show score. Kinda.
&42 So yes...I'm kinda proud of the music in this scene.
&43 So the subway music is more for a tense, but not directly violent situation. It's very hard to do this in adventure games, as there IS no action.
&44 So really having a "pulse" of something that is happening, along with some peaks in the music works really well for this scene.
&45 You can hear the pulse in the pizzicato, as was as the staccato strings. The peaks are done by the brass at times with slow crescendos.
&46 It fits the dialogue and situation, but doesn't directly say "action is happening". More like...well there is a bomb and you are trying to defuse it.
&47 What a deliciously gruesome scene. This wasn't even this bad at first when I wrote the track. Later on MORE gore was added.
&48 This particular track is important just to show that "oh my god" feeling, and that is what it seems to do.
&49 Also James added to the impact by having the room be dark at first, which was not in the first few builds.
&50 So turning on the light, right on the impact in the music, is even more effective.
&51 This is another scene that had various "pieces" of the music in separate tracks. Each track builds in succession.
&52 This was meant to occur on the growls from the emanation that appears through this scene.
&53 While I probably didn't need to do several tracks, it does give James the ability to move things around if he needs to.
&54 And also for any that decide to click through a  few pieces of dialogue, the music moves with that as well.
&55 This particular music was important, because CEL is a very iconic vision for Technobabylon.
&56 A police/science/tech hybrid that is super clean, with shiny metal surfaces, and lots of...blue.
&57 So this music was kind of meant to reflect that as being a technological marvel.
&58 I don't have much more than that, really I was just trying to write something cool :)
&59 There are three main characters in this game, you have Regis, Lao, and Latha.
&60 However, in some ways I feel Central is the main character of this game.
&61 So engineering the voice for Central was quite important. I didn't just want a standard computer voice.
&62 I wanted something that would reflect that Central's origin is in fact, human.
&63 So we ended up with sort of a human/computer hybrid voice, which is essentially a pitched down vocal to start with.
&64 Mainly because the original voice was kind of adorable. But her acting was very computer like, so pitching her down actually worked well.
&65 You couldn't just say words and it would work, you had to act it out properly with the proper inflections.
&66 And the actress probably doesn't even know her voice has been altered in such a way yet.
&67 So after changing the pitch, autofilter was added, some chorus, and some delay, along with some pitch correction to make it sound artificial.
&68 And there you have it. Central.
&69 This entire section was meant to be pretty. It was meant to be almost like you are in a jungle, or the amazon.
&70 That is exactly what the description James had for me in terms of music.
&71 So I ended up with this New Age style theme, with a bit of sci-fi.
&72 But it's also topped off by some angelic choir, which just seals the deal for this track for me.
&73 This room is loud. It was meant to be.
&74 This sound is this room is borrowed from Gemini Rue from the Weather Tower, which was some sort of print press ambience in real life.
&75 But I added my gas furnace for color!
&76 This is my voice!
&77 It's basically the same effects as Central, but with a male voice.
&78 Obviously I pitched myself down, but the effect is there. And I did it in a more condescending authoritative way.
&79 The very last battle in Gemini Rue involved a percussion based track with very simple background ambience. Using a lot of Taikos.
&80 So this music is actually kind of the same idea, but a little more interesting. It has more of a cyberpunk feel to it.
&81 But on top of that, the main melody is more pleasant, using humming choir, and some synth pads, as well as bells.
&82 While some rather heavy percussion and synth bass is playing in the background.
&83 This adds to the scene a great deal, but doesn't go over the top. Because as I said, there is no real "action" in point-and-clicks.
&84 So instead you just have to make things very tense. And after the music was added to this scene, it definitely does that.
&85 The laser is a small part of this game, but it was really important I make this thing sound interesting.
&86 That sort of "glass cutting sound" along with the musical hum is exactly what I was going for, and it took quite a bit of time to get this.
&87 In fact, it kind of reminds me of the hyperspace jump sound from Homeworld. Which also was quite musical in a way.
&88 So every time someone uses this, it's a bit more pleasant than "Pewwwwwwww!"
&89 All three soldiers in this game are Dave's voice. Each one is pitched slightly so it appears to be a different person.
&90 The hardest part was figuring out the sound of the voice, and what effects would accomplish that sound.
&91 The soliders were meant to be kinda faceless, and have all personality erased. So a bit of ring modulation and other effects took care of that.
&92 The voices are heard, and can be understood, but you can't quite hear the inflections in the voice that give it personality.
&93 Therefore it achieves that sort of "storm trooper" effect. Or a better reference would be the Combine from Half Life 2.
&94 This track is probably one of my favorite tracks I've done, as it takes a very simple chord progression and makes it interesting.
&95 The track has this whole seedy undertone which fit the whole "downtown" appearance in this scene.
&96 The psudeo east coast drum loop added with the pulsing synth bass, going back and forth between two chords in the whole song.
&97 But is also topped off with a very lite synth bell finish.
&98 EDM. Such a hard genre of music to do. Most people don't realize this, and in some cases don't believe it, But EDM and pop is hard.
&99 It's less about the musical writing, and more about sound design. You can come up with a great chord progression and a hook.
&100 But it falls flat if you don't know all the bells and whistles to put in between.
&101 This is essentially the EDM version of the Technobabylon theme. It doesn't sound commercial, but it does have a uniqueness to it.
&102 And I personally like it. That it doesn't sound like commercial dance music.
&103 Oh man. This track. This is the last one I did for Technobabylon. While this track is only about a minute long it took 4 hours to do.
&104 As a comparison, it took like 45 minutes to do the title music in this game.
&105 I postponed it so much because I kept getting ideas. First I thought chip tune music. But then I said no to that, because everyone does chip tune music.
&106 Then I thought, why not get the soundsets for the Sega Genesis? But that turned out to be a bit difficult, and required some fast learning.
&107 Then I remember I did a track a long time ago for a client, known as "Oxhorn" which actually was a bit of a j-pop parody.
&108 It lasted only about 15 seconds, but was hilarious. And that is what James and Dave wanted. So I went into that style for this track.
&109 And this is the result!
&110 The music here isn't exactly music, but it incorporates two sound effect that are known in this type of universe.
&111 At first you hear the geiger counter clicks, and then later the vintage WW2 air raid siren.
&112 Basically, I was going for a Fallout vibe.
&113 The classical piano in the back is performed by Jennifer Thomas.
&114 I always wanted to use Moonlight Sonata in a project, it's probably my favorite classical piece of all time (aside from the Planets of course)
&115 And I felt it really fit here. Because you have a bunch of higher ups, in a glamorous restaurant, eating...human flesh.
&116 Adding this piece of music just makes the whole scene that much more morbid.
&117 Also as a Sound Design note, you'll hear the tone of the track change a bit as you move from room to room.
&118 When I first saw the Aerostat drawings, I understood that this is the future, but not everything changes.
&119 We see this today, with tablets in our hands. Something even more advanced than the padds in Star Trek.
&120 So I feel the Aerostat would fall behind a bit in technology. So I chose the sounds to make the aircraft sound like a turboprop.
&121 The take-off, landing, and idle sounds are various combinations of jet engines and props, as well as a few samples of the Bombardier Q400.
&122 This scene had to be loud and dangerous sounding, as well as dynamic.
&123 So I had two sounds layered here. The overall background ambience of engines, wind, and props.
&124 Combined with the loud engine on the left.
&125 When you stop the engine on the left, you'll notice that goes away, and now you can hear the wind and other engines.
&126 It's not every day that I get to create sound design depicting a man getting chewed to death in a bunch of machinery.
&127 Lots of rattling, bone crunching, and 'glop' sounds make this a bit more graphic than it looks.
&128 The chair room is essentially the life blood of Central. Lots of organic uh...balloons lining the walls. Very creepy looking.
&129 So I wanted to show that in the sound design. You'll notice you can hear sort of digital glitches on the left.
&130 And a bit of...sloppiness on the right.
&131 All backed by a pulsing heartbeat like drone.
&132 The core music here has a very technological sound. In fact, the piece itself is written in 5/4 time.
&133 But the chords I chose don't actually have thirds in them, they are all sus2 chords, which actually kind of gives it a Chrono Trigger vibe.
&134 There are three versions of this track. One in this room, the other within Trance, and a third track which is a more ambient version.
&135 This scene shows a bunch of remnants of all the people that the Mindjacker has killed. I wanted to reflect that in the sound design here.
&136 Most people wouldn't hear it, but the odd sounds you are hearing are actually dialogue from the game.
&137 This scene worked ok with the current core music, but the emotional impact wasn't there.
&138 So I wanted to do a sort of similar feeling that you would hear in a movie.
&139 A simple recurring motif, which in this case is the piano, along with some moving chords, utilizing strings.
&140 I couldn't go too far as it would overcome the dialogue that was happening.
&141 But the idea was to make the player believe that Regis was sacrificing himself, and that was the end of it.
&142 Of course, just afterwards you find out that wasn't the case.
